visuals.heading: What Political Science Actually Opens Up

items.text: A political science degree is not a narrow ticket to one government exam.
Clearing the entry filter does not end the climb, it starts a new one.
This is the track most political science students never hear about, and it is the one with the most genuine room to scale.
Beyond campaign firms, independent policy consultants advise companies, associations, and sometimes government bodies directly on regulatory strategy.

Why this scales when the others don't: you set your own pricing instead of sitting on a fixed pay band, demand repeats every election cycle rather than depending on one employer's budget, and once you have a track record you can bring on junior researchers instead of doing every hour of work yourself.
Before you commit real years, an exam attempt, a PhD, an unpaid internship season, a law degree, run the track you are leaning toward through The four questions.
Policy research and academia reward people who genuinely enjoy long solitary reading and writing.
UPSC preparation, a self-funded PhD, and unpaid think-tank internships all assume months to years of low or no income while you build the credential.

blocks.heading: Building Proof Before You Commit Years

items.text: A qualification checklist tells you what is formally required.
Do not start UPSC prep, enrol in a PhD, or take a law-entrance coaching package before passing all three proofs below.
One published op-ed, one policy brief written to a real institution's format, or one data-backed research note on a specific issue, not a general statement that you "like current affairs."
Families default to civil services because it is the option everyone has heard of, not because it has the best growth curve.
A funded seat, a realistic timeline, and an honest look at how many recent graduates from your target department actually got permanent posts matter more than the prestige of the university name.
Constitutional law, regulatory law, and public policy sit right next to political science.

blocks.heading: Track 4: Policy Research and Think Tanks

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Current Payscale India data for Policy Analyst roles shows entry-level pay (under one year) averaging around ₹3.4 lakh a year, rising to roughly ₹5 lakh in the one-to-four-year range, with an overall average near ₹5.9 lakh. It is not a high-paying entry point on its own, its real value is that it is the training ground that feeds directly into Tracks 1, 2, and 9: consulting, corporate government affairs, and academia all hire people who can already write a clean policy brief.

blocks.heading: Track 5: Journalism and Political Commentary

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Entry-level journalism pay in India commonly runs ₹15,000-25,000 a month, rising to roughly ₹50,000-1,00,000 a month for senior reporters and editors with five to ten years of experience - a real but modest employed-track ceiling. An independent platform built around the same beat - a political newsletter, an explainer channel, or a niche commentary practice, follows the same ownership logic as Track 1 above, and can outgrow an employed newsroom salary entirely for someone who builds a real audience and reporting credibility.

blocks.heading: UPSC/IFS and Academia

figures.label: Exam Candidate Count
figures.source: In the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2025, roughly 10-11 lakh people applied. About 14,000 cleared the prelims, roughly 13,000 sat the mains, about 2,800 were interviewed, and 958 candidates were finally recommended for 1,087 vacancies, a selection rate close to 1 in 1,000 applicants.

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Getting recommended is not the finish line. An IAS or IPS officer starts on a fixed Level 10 basic pay of ₹56,100 a month. The real climb runs through eight more pay levels over a career of roughly 37 years, up to a single Cabinet Secretary post at ₹2,50,000 a month. Most officers in any entering batch never reach the top rungs, postings, cadre allocation, and empanelment for senior posts are their own, separate competition.

blocks.heading: College and Degree Decision, an Honest Take

items.text: Newer private liberal-arts universities, Ashoka, O.P.

Test any spending above the conservative starting benchmark of roughly 10% of your total education budget against real, course-specific evidence: does the private option's faculty, internship pipeline, and peer network create an advantage you genuinely cannot build yourself through a public-college department plus deliberate outside work, think-tank internships, published writing, or a strong political-science reading list.

supporting: Newer private liberal-arts universities, Ashoka, O.P. Jindal Global University, FLAME, Symbiosis, pitch smaller class sizes, global exposure, and stronger placement support, at a genuinely different price: often ₹8-15 lakh or more for the full undergraduate programme.

blocks.heading: AI Is Doing to Political Science Careers

items.text: Routine, first-pass policy-brief drafting, turning a bill or committee report into a plain-language summary, is already shifting into AI-assisted workflows at many think tanks and corporate-affairs teams.

Wire-style, fact-based political reporting (rewriting a press release, reporting a routine result) is easier to automate than beat reporting or investigation, so junior "content mill" journalism roles carry more exposure.

Basic legislative research triage, finding which bills, committees, or notifications touch a specific sector, is now largely a database-search problem AI tools handle faster than a fresher can by hand.

blocks.heading: Skills That Matter on Every Track

items.text: Research and argument construction, the core skill every track above shares.
Data literacy, comfort reading survey data, election results, and government datasets.
Clear, plain-language writing, a policy brief, an op-ed, or a client memo is worthless if only other specialists can follow it. This is the proof format most of these tracks actually hire on.
Negotiation and coalition-building, the human layer behind consulting, diplomacy, and corporate government affairs that AI does not touch.
A working foreign language, a genuine differentiator for IFS, multilateral, and international-relations-adjacent roles specifically, less critical for the domestic tracks.
Practical AI fluency, using AI tools to speed up research and drafting while personally verifying every output, per the AI section above.
Geography is also a popular UPSC optional.
